title: HuntOutput
description: Output of one Hunt task: zero-or-more findings plus coverage gaps.

evidence_snippet.description: Verbatim code excerpt that demonstrates the flaw.

poc.description: The proof-of-concept the hunter wrote and ran. Everything in here is the hunter's ACCOUNT of what it did — it is evidence, not a verdict. Whether the PoC proved anything is decided in Python by pyhunt.oracle.gate from run_output, and written to the sibling `execution` object.

run_output.description: REQUIRED, and must be the COMPLETE combined stdout+stderr of the observed run, verbatim and unsummarised. The [PYHUNT-OBSERVER] marker lines in it are the only input the execution gate has. Paraphrasing this field, or trimming it to 'the interesting part', destroys the proof.

succeeded.description: YOUR BELIEF about whether the exploit worked, based on the PoC's own assertions. It does NOT decide the finding's status and it never promotes a finding: pyhunt.oracle.gate re-reads run_output and rules independently. Answer it honestly rather than optimistically — a claim the evidence does not support is logged as an over-claim, which is how prompt drift is detected.

hedged_language.description: Set true if the description uses 'might'/'could'/'possibly' — flags noise for triage.

needs_poc.description: Set true when execution was not available (execution_available=false, or the toolchain was missing) so this finding rests on a static source->sink argument. Do NOT set it to mean 'my PoC did not work' — the execution gate records that outcome itself, and it never deletes a finding.

execution.description: COMPUTED BY PYHUNT — never emit this field. Any value supplied here is overwritten by the execution gate. Documented so the shape is visible to anyone reading the schema.

proven.description: True only for outcome=proven. The single field that means 'confirmed by execution'.

evidence.description: The marker lines that carried the decision.

task_id.description: The hunt task that produced this finding. Injected by findings_io.record_finding and preserved by apply-proofs / apply-structural: coverage.py attributes findings to tasks through it, and the payload nonce is derived from (run_id, task_id), so a finding that loses it becomes unreplayable and uncountable.

structural_probe.description: A DECLARATIVE probe for a class the audit hook cannot see (codegen injection, algorithmic complexity, shared-state contamination, unhandled crashes, and — via `flow_witness` — every class CPython raises no audit event for at all: SQL injection, XSS, open redirect, SSTI, log and header injection). Data only: a dotted callable, a benign input, a hostile input. There is deliberately nowhere here to put code — PyHunt's own harness supplies the assertion, which is what makes a structural verdict worth more than a PoC that grades its own homework. Run `python3 scripts/structural.py kinds` for the vocabulary.

target.description: Dotted import path of the callable under test. It MUST resolve inside the target — a callable outside the target roots fails condition S-2 and the probe is discarded.

construct.description: Optional class to instantiate before calling `target`'s final attribute as a method.

benign_args.description: Positional arguments for the CONTROL run. Place the literal $PYHUNT_BENIGN where the untrusted value goes; the harness mints that marker itself so the control cannot be chosen to collide with the payload.

hostile_args.description: Positional arguments for the ATTACK run. Place the literal $PYHUNT_NONCE inside the payload; the harness substitutes this run's nonce. For kind=codegen_ast this is mandatory — the claim is that *this* string became code.

attribute.description: kind=state_mutation: dotted path of the module global being contaminated.

expected_value.description: kind=state_mutation: the value the attacker's input should install.

expected_exceptions.description: kind=exception_escape: exception type names that count as an escaping crash.

input_builder.description: kind=growth_curve: a size-parameterised input from the closed builder vocabulary (repeat_str, list_of, nested_list, nested_dict, repeat_key, json_text).

sizes.description: kind=growth_curve: ascending ladder, at least three rungs — two points are a line, and a line is not a curve.

rationale.description: One sentence: why this differential is the right measurement for this defect.

entry_args.description: flow_witness: positional arguments for the PUBLIC ENTRY POINT. Must contain `$PYHUNT_NONCE` somewhere — the sentinel is the whole mechanism; without it the tracer cannot tell the attacker's value from any other string the target is holding.

entry_kwargs.description: flow_witness: keyword arguments for the entry point. `$PYHUNT_NONCE` may live here instead of in entry_args.

sink_location.description: flow_witness: the claimed sink as `file:line`, exact. The verdict is the claim that the sentinel is live in THAT frame at THAT line, so an approximate location makes the result meaningless.

intercept.description: sink_semantics: dotted path to the DANGEROUS CALLABLE to intercept (sqlite3.Cursor.execute, builtins.open, requests.get). The harness wraps it so it captures its arguments and raises — the operation is never performed.

argument.description: sink_semantics: which argument of the intercepted callable carries the payload — a positional index or a keyword name.

semantics.description: sink_semantics: which grammar decides whether the payload arrived as STRUCTURE or as data.

root.description: sink_semantics, `path` analyser only: the directory the path was supposed to stay inside.

privileged_args.description: differential_response: arguments for the PRIVILEGED principal — the call that legitimately sees the sentinel.

privileged_kwargs.description: differential_response: keyword arguments for the privileged principal.

unprivileged_args.description: differential_response: arguments for the principal that should NOT see it.

unprivileged_kwargs.description: differential_response: keyword arguments for the unprivileged principal.

sentinel.description: differential_response: the value only the privileged caller should receive. Defaults to the run nonce.

expected_type.description: type_selection: the fully-qualified type the caller asked for, as `module.QualName`. Anything else coming back is the finding.

file.description: config_assertion: repo-relative path to the configuration or workflow file. Absolute paths and `..` are refused.

path.description: config_assertion: dotted/indexed path into the parsed document, e.g. `jobs.release.environment`.

assertion.description: config_assertion: the single check to evaluate. Closed vocabulary — a spec cannot express 'run this predicate'.

expected.description: config_assertion: the value or regex the assertion compares against.

structural.description: COMPUTED BY PYHUNT — never emit this field. The structural oracle's verdict, attached by findings_io apply-structural. `demonstrated` is NOT `proven`: report_build counts them under separate denominators, and only the execution gate can promote.

refuted.description: A deterministic demonstration that the defence works. Never deletes the finding; phase 2c must address it in writing.

gaps_observed.description: Areas the hunter could not fully examine — feeds Gapfill.

files_read.description: Repo-relative paths this unit ACTUALLY opened, one entry per file. W4.2: the coverage ledger is input-level, so a task naming five files could be answered by an agent that opened two and nothing downstream could tell. Phase 3 asserts every task's target_files appear here. Report what you opened, not what you were assigned — an honest short list is a gap with a name, an inflated one is a false coverage claim.
